summary.name: SourceHut
summary.one_liner: SourceHut is a suite of open source software development tools covering git and Mercurial hosting, CI builds, mailing lists, ticket tracking, IRC chat, and wikis, offered as a public alpha.
use_cases: hosting private or public git repositories
running virtualised CI builds for software projects
managing patch review over mailing lists
hosting an IRC bouncer and chat logs
summary.what_it_does: SourceHut is a set of tools for software project maintainers and collaborators. It provides git repository hosting (with first-class Mercurial support) including public, private and unlisted repos and fine-grained access control that works for users without accounts. Its CI runs fully virtualised builds on various Linux distros and BSDs, with ad-hoc job submission, post-build triggers, and SSH login after failures. Mailing list tools support patch review on the web, searchable archives, and work powered by git send-email. It also offers ticket tracking limited to actionable tasks, a hosted IRC bouncer with a web chat, Markdown and git-driven wikis, and the hut CLI for exporting data and running GraphQL queries.
notable: Works without JavaScript and with no tracking, advertising or AI features
Mailing-list-driven patch review and ticket tracking via email, with or without an account
Full data export via hut CLI and option to move to a self-hosted SourceHut instance
caveats: Currently available as a public alpha
Alpha status means expectations should be limited
